chain.label: Route 4 placed near runway 33 approach path
chain.trigger: FAA placed Helicopter Route 4 in close proximity to the runway 33 approach path at DCA without procedural mitigations to separate helicopter and fixed-wing traffic

chain.label: FAA failed to review routes, normalized visual separation
chain.trigger: the FAA ATO did not regularly review or reevaluate the route as required...failed to act on recommendations...contributed to a gradual normalization of using pilot-applied visual separation

chain.label: Army did not train pilots on altimeter error tolerances
chain.trigger: the Army did not ensure that helicopter pilots were adequately informed about the effects of allowable error tolerances in barometric altimeters

chain.label: Additive altimeter error, worsened by ESSS
chain.trigger: position error of 50 ft for an ESSS-equipped helicopter...cumulative effects of these errors and corrections could account for the difference between displayed and true altitude

chain.label: PAT25 flew above Route 4's maximum altitude
chain.trigger: the accident helicopter crew was flying above the published maximum route altitude

caused_by.evidence: Army did not ensure...pilots were adequately informed about the effects of allowable error tolerances
the crew of PAT25 observed a barometric altimeter altitude about 100 ft lower than the helicopter's true altitude

chain.label: Combined LC/HC positions degraded controller performance
chain.trigger: high workload at the DCA air traffic control tower degraded controller performance and situation awareness...contributed to misprioritization of duties, incomplete traffic advisories, and the lack of safety alerts to both flight crews

caused_by.evidence: reliance on pilot-applied visual separation...contributed to a gradual normalization of using pilot-applied visual separation

chain.label: Helicopter radio reception degraded by static
chain.trigger: the transmissions made by PAT25 were accompanied by static interference, making intelligibility difficult

chain.label: PAT25 crew missed 'circling' in traffic advisory
chain.trigger: the helicopter's CVR recording captured this transmission as...and did not contain the word 'circling'

caused_by.evidence: transmissions made by PAT25 were accompanied by static interference, making intelligibility difficult

chain.label: Mic key blocked 'pass behind' instruction
chain.trigger: one of the helicopter pilots pressed the radio push-to-talk switch for 0.8 seconds, blocking the words 'two five pass behind that'

chain.label: Neither aircraft had effective collision-avoidance alerting
chain.trigger: the helicopter was not equipped with any integrated traffic awareness or collision avoidance technology...RAs are inhibited below 900 ft agl during descent

chain.label: PAT25 crew requested visual separation without positive ID
chain.trigger: PAT25 has the traffic in sight request visual separation...the IP did not positively identify flight 5342 at the time of the initial traffic advisory

caused_by.evidence: reinforced an incorrect expectation that the airplane did not pose a conflict
blocked the helicopter crew from receiving the 'pass behind' portion of the controller's instruction
helicopter was not equipped with any integrated traffic awareness or collision avoidance technology

chain.label: Flight 5342 crew did not detect helicopter until impact
chain.trigger: the crew of flight 5342 did not detect the helicopter until about 1 second before impact

caused_by.evidence: the lack of a required traffic advisory from the controller...contributed to the airplane crew's lack of timely awareness
the crew did not receive this type of alert and was, therefore, unaware of the severity of the conflict

chain.label: PAT25 and flight 5342 collided over the Potomac River
chain.trigger: the aircraft collided over the Potomac River at an altitude about 278 ft above mean sea level

caused_by.evidence: this vertical separation decreases the further from the shoreline the helicopter is flown
lack of effective pilot-applied visual separation by the helicopter crew, which resulted in a midair collision
the crew of flight 5342 did not see the helicopter until it was too late to avoid a collision

chain.label: All 67 occupants of both aircraft were killed
chain.trigger: The 2 pilots, 2 flight attendants, and 60 passengers on board the airplane and all 3 crewmembers on board the helicopter died. Both aircraft were destroyed

caused_by.evidence: Both aircraft were destroyed as a result of the accident
